The clouds are so dark that you worry it might rain, which could hinder the excavation. Walking a short distance to campus, your favorite music careens through your earbuds, loud enough to drown any nearby chatter and whatever other noises of the outside world. This brief journey allows you time to bask in the calm between your school life and home life. Though she mainly stays in her room now, Mikah used to preach about setting time apart to connect with nature. <br><br> The leaves on the trees lining the streets have turned color, leaving a red carpet of foliage blanketing your path to school. The beauty to be found in death and decay rattles around in your mind, almost undercutting your excitement about the excavation. Before long, the university bus pulling in to the library's bus stop pierces through your musical meditation. <br><br> (link:"Continue")[ (replace:?passageText)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ You arrive at a huddle of your students at the parking lot behind the library, the designated meeting spot for today's class. Plucking out your earbuds, you see one of your students, Maya, smiling and waving at you. She is a senior in your class with plenty of potential and a fire in her eyes that's impossible to ignore. You know she is shooting for the Teaching Assistant position after you graduate and you wholeheartedly believe she deserves it. Before you can return her greeting, Dr. Howard pulls up in his white minivan with his window down, sticking his head out to shout joyfully in a volume almost criminal for such an early hour in the day. <br><br> "Good morning, class! Are we all ready to head out?" <br><br> He gets an affirmative cheer from the students, some of which are a lot more enthused than others. He rolls his window up, cutting the engine as the bus slides its doors open. <br><br> (link:"Board the bus")[ (replace:?passageText)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ Boarding the bus, you embark on a lengthy drive to the dig. Passing Aylesbury Pike, you watch through the window as chicken houses and free-roaming livestock flash by. You don't pay the road much attention, as your mind is already at your destination. Your research shows the area to be a strange location for the uncovered ruins, with a puzzling disconnect between where history implies they should be and where they emerged. It's too early to theorize about anything: researchers, archaeologists, and historians alike are still figuring it out. <br><br> The bus finally pulls up to an enormous field of soft, green grass extending far into the horizon. The terrain dips in the middle into a huge, rectangular hole, alive with the rumbling of machinery and the clacking of tools. You recognize a few faces on site: a couple of renowned archeologists from other universities, a geologist you recall studying a book he wrote a few semesters back and hating every word. Dr. Howard steps off of the bus to engage in small talk with the lot. <br><br> (link:"Alight from the bus")[ (replace:?passageText)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ Stepping out with the rest of the students, you keep them in check until the professor returns to guide the tour. Once he does, you notice a look of pure delight on his face. <br><br> "Great news! We get to take some of these relics back with us to study them at length. God, I was worried for a second we'd have to fight over them! Have you seen these academics clamoring for a piece like vultures?" <br><br> You smirk at the professor's unapologetic disdain for his colleagues. It's the product of competitive, scientific curiosity and you admire his passion. <br><br> After reviewing guidelines for digsite Do's and Don'ts, Dr. Howard leads the tour. He explains the technicalities of the excavation, the estimated era of the findings, and the historical value of these artifacts. Your excitement builds, wondering what stories they might tell. <br><br> (link:"Continue")[ (replace:?passageText)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ "Obviously, we're tragically under-informed about the history behind these ruins. It's hypothesized that the inhibitors in this region worshiped a powerful, malicious entity with ambiguous connections to ancient gods of fertility and fornication. You'll see the artifacts have a certain theme to them, and I invite you to make your own conclusion so long as it's supported with sound logic." <br><br> The professor then leads the group to a table with several items laid out across it. He describes some phallic statuettes and grotesque bloated ones. A large ring made of what appears to be melted black rock, with large thorns adorning it, shaped to resemble a crown. <br><br> (link:"Inspect the artifacts")[ (track: 'beautifulPiano', 'fadeout', 3) (track: 'artifact', 'fadein', 3) (track: 'artifact', 'loop', true) (replace:?entirePassage)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ <div id="centeredImage"> =|= (print: '<img style="height: 18em; width: auto;" src="images/objects/crown.png">') =|= (print: '<img style="height: 18em"; width: auto;" src="images/objects/fertility.png">') |==| </div> (live:3s)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ The crowd moves on, but you're too transfixed by the artifacts to follow. <br><br> (link:"Inspect closer")[ (replace:?entirePassage)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ <div id="centeredImage"> (print: '<img style="height: 23em; width: auto;" src="images/objects/crown.png">') </div> <div id="fsfx"> (print: '<img style="opacity: 0.2;" src="images/other/corruptred100.png">') </div> (live:3s)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ <br><br> (link:"Continue")[ (go-to:"Field Trip Pt2") ] (stop:) ] ] ] (stop:) ] ] ] ] ] ] ] ] ] ] ] ] }{ (set: _sizePassageText to $sizeText's 31st) (set: _sizeText46 to $sizeText's 46th) (display:"passageText") (replace:?passageText)[ For a moment, the crown-shaped artifact is all you can see and the world blurs around it. It's the most beautiful thing you've ever laid your eyes on, its thorns so smooth on the edges and razor-sharp at the tips, its color so mesmerizing. You long to touch it, to feel its texture against the pads of your finger. With a dizzying intensity, you wonder if you're worthy. You're not sure of what, and you don't spare the 'what' a thought. You reach toward it when a tap on your shoulder almost makes you jump. <br><br> You find Maya standing behind you, her arm outstretched, her hand suspended in the air an inch away from your chest. Her shoulder-length, wavy black hair curtains an expression of concern that is directed at you, though you can't comprehend why. <br><br> (link:"Speak with Maya")[ (replace:?entirePassage)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ (set: _activeCharacter to $maya) (display:"Character Presence") (replace:?doll)[ (print: '<img class="layer4" src="images/npc/maya/bust.png">') ] (hide:?interactionBox) (replace:?dialogueBox)+(text-size:_sizePassageText)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ "Are you okay? Concerns on Campus'' <br> (text-size:0.6)[ ''_staffWriter'', Staff Writer ] <hr> ] (text-size:0.62)[ ''The Rising Threat'' <br><br> According to campus security, there have been at least five reported incidents of students being robbed or having their belongings stolen near the library over the past month. These robberies have targeted students studying late at night. In a few cases, students have been physically threatened or intimidated by suspects who quickly fled the scene. <br><br> "I was just walking out after working late on an assignment, when someone came up behind me and grabbed my bag," said a sophomore who asked to remain anonymous. "It all happened so fast. By the time I stood up and tried to shout, the thief was already gone." <br><br> ''A Safe Space No Longer?'' <br><br> The library has long been seen as one of the most famous places on campus, with its historical significance and steady flow of students throughout the day. It has been a go-to spot for students looking for a quiet place to study, read, or catch up on homework. However, as these recent incidents unfold, many students are now questioning whether their once-trusted study haven can be considered a safe space. <br><br> "I've always felt comfortable in the library, but now I'm second-guessing it," said Maria Lopez, a senior who frequents the library late in the evening. "I've heard about the robberies, and now I'm worried about leaving my things unattended, even for a minute." <br><br> ''Campus Response'' <br><br> In response to the spike in library-related crimes, campus security has ramped up patrols around the area, especially during late hours. The administration has also issued a statement reminding students to remain vigilant and to keep an eye on their personal belongings at all times. <br><br> "We are aware of the recent thefts and are taking immediate steps to address the situation," said Vivian Lawson of the University Police Department. "In addition to increased patrols, we are also looking into adding more lighting around the entrances to deter criminal activity." <br><br> Campus officials are also advising students to report any suspicious behavior immediately, and to be cautious when studying late at night, particularly in less trafficked areas of the library. <br><br> ''Student Reactions'' <br><br> While some students appreciate the increased security measures, others feel that more needs to be done to prevent such crimes from occurring in the first place. A number of students have suggested that the library extend its hours and have more staff present during late-night periods. Others are calling for the installation of security cameras inside the library to monitor activity more closely. <br><br> "I think the library should invest in better security infrastructure," said Alex Chen, a junior who has used the library regularly for years. "If they can make sure that people feel safe, then I'd be more willing to study late without constantly looking over my shoulder." <br><br> ''How to Stay Safe'' <br><br> For students who find themselves studying late in the library, campus security recommends the following safety tips: <br> * Keep your belongings close: Don't leave backpacks, phones, or laptops unattended. Always take your valuables with you or lock them in a secure location when you leave your desk. * Be aware of your surroundings: Stay alert to the people around you, especially if you notice anyone acting suspiciously. * Travel in groups: If possible, walk to and from the library with friends, particularly during the late evening hours. * Use campus security: If you feel unsafe or notice anything suspicious, contact campus security immediately at the designated emergency number. <br> ''Conclusion'' <br><br> While the recent spike in robberies near the library is concerning, it is important that students, staff, and campus security work together to restore a sense of safety to this crucial part of campus. By staying vigilant and following safety guidelines, students can continue to use the library as a valuable resource for their academic success, without compromising their personal security. <br><br> As the investigation into these crimes continues, it is clear that the library, like any other public space, can only be as safe as the collective effort to keep it secure. It's up to all of us to ensure that our campus remains a place where learning and safety go hand in hand. ] }{ (set: _activeCharacter to $police) (display:"passageText") (replace:?passageText)[ (set:$time to it +1) (if: _touch is "Light")[ (display:"posArousalMid") ] (else:)[ (display:"posArousalMax") ] (display:"Save NPC Changes") "Excuse me?!" Sweat forms on her brow as she slides her hand back around her ass and gives it a little smack. <br><br> "What is happening to me?" she moans, reaching up to unbutton the top buttons of her uniform. <br><br> She lets go of your wrists, opting to fondle her own breasts for a moment before regaining her composure. "I'm sorry, this is unprofessional. This is... I... I can't think straight. Just go, get out of here." <br> (link:"Leave")[ (go-to:"Campus") ] ] ] }{ (text-size:0.9)[ ''A Campus United: Two Years After the Tragedy'' <br> (text-size:0.6)[ ''_staffWriter'', Staff Writer ] <hr> ] (text-size:0.62)[ Two years ago, the student body of Miskatonic University experienced an unimaginable tragedy that shook our entire community to its core. A string of disappearances culminated in the discovery of several missing students' bodies, found in various locations on campus. The weight of those events cast a long, dark shadow over our school, leaving us all with questions, grief, and fear. But in the aftermath of this crisis, our community has shown remarkable resilience and strength. As we reflect on these past two years, we are reminded not only of the darkness we've faced but also of the light we've found together. <br><br> ''A Crisis Unfolds'' <br><br> In the early months of that dreadful year, our campus was rocked by the inexplicable disappearances of several students. The once-bustling halls became eerily silent as rumors spread, and fear began to permeate every corner of the school. For weeks, the community was left in limbo, unsure of what was happening or who could be trusted. The days stretched into months before the terrifying discovery of the missing bodies in hidden corners of our campus. The loss was incomprehensible, and the sense of violation, knowing that such horrors could happen right under our noses, left a deep scar on the entire student body. <br><br> As the authorities worked to uncover the details surrounding the disappearances, we, the students, were left to navigate the emotional aftermath. The tragedy prompted many difficult conversations about safety, trust, and how we, as a community, could heal from the trauma. <br><br> ''A Community in Mourning'' <br><br> In the wake of the tragedy, the school went into a period of mourning. Students and staff alike attended memorials, shared stories, and supported one another in the months following the discovery. The missing students, identified as Laura Kane (Anthropology, sophomore), William Price (Physics, junior), and Nadia Vasquez (Literature, freshman), were last seen in their respective dorms by friends and roommates. <br><br> ''University Response'' <br><br> Campus officials, while urging calm, have acknowledged the seriousness of the situation. "We are working closely with local law enforcement and campus security to investigate these incidents," said Dean Abigail Halsey in a statement released earlier today. "The safety and well-being of our students remain our utmost priority." <br><br> ''Eerie Reports and Student Fears'' <br><br> However, whispers of something more sinister have begun circulating among the student body. Many students have taken to social media to share their fears, with some claiming to hear strange noises in the halls at night- knockings against walls and shambling down the halls. "I woke up to my window open even though I had locked it," said Erica Fielding, a roommate of one of the missing students. "It was freezing." <br><br> ''Call for Information'' <br><br> Authorities have asked anyone with information regarding the missing students to come forward. Tips can be submitted anonymously to the Campus Security Hotline or the Arkham Police Department. <br><br> For now, the fates of the students remain a chilling mystery, leaving many to grapple with a question that grows more haunting by the day: Who- or what- is behind these disappearances? ] }{ (text-size:0.9)[ ''Vanishing Students: A Growing Concern'' <br> (text-size:0.6)[ ''_staffWriter'', Staff Writer ] <hr> ] (text-size:0.62)[ ''A Blanket of Fog Over Arkham'' <br><br> Miskatonic University has been shrouded in an unusually persistent fog lately, with many students noting its eerie presence. While meteorologists attribute the phenomenon to seasonal humidity and cooler temperatures, others believe the fog's pervasive nature has more than just meteorological implications. <br><br> ''Psychological Effects of Foggy Conditions'' <br><br> Fog has long been associated with feelings of disorientation and unease. "Low visibility can disrupt our spatial awareness, leading to heightened anxiety," explained Dr. Emily Cartwright, a professor of psychology. "This kind of weather creates a natural veil, obscuring our surroundings and, in some cases, even our higher reasoning." <br><br> Students have reported difficulty concentrating and a general sense of malaise. "It feels like the fog is pressing down on me," said Sarah Leland, a junior in the Philosophy department. "Like it's not just around us but inside us somehow." <br><br> ''Folklore and Perceptions'' <br><br> Fog also holds a place in local folklore, often symbolizing mystery and concealment. Tales from Arkham's past speak of figures emerging from the mist, only to vanish again without a trace. While such stories are dismissed as superstition, they remain a topic of fascination, particularly in times like these. <br><br> ''Coping With the Gloom'' <br><br> Experts recommend staying active and maintaining routines to counter the psychological effects of foggy weather. "Make an effort to seek out brighter spaces during the day," advised Dr. Cartwright. "And remember, this weather will pass- it always does." <br><br> For now, the fog remains a constant presence, quietly influencing life at Miskatonic University. Whether its effects are merely atmospheric or something more remains an open question, one that lingers in the minds of students as they navigate the haze. ] }{ (text-size:0.9)[ ''Miskatonic Sauna Session Takes a Dark Turn'' <br> (text-size:0.6)[ ''_staffWriter'', Staff Writer ] <hr> ] (text-size:0.62)[ ''Chaos at the Recreation Center'' <br><br> Late last Friday evening, what began as a typical visit to the sauna at Miskatonic University's Recreation Center turned into a perplexing mystery. Five students, identified as members of the university's Philosophy club, entered the sauna for a routine relaxation session. Mind-splitting pleasures for some, and unfathomable fates for others. <br><br> ''The Order of Vhl'Attar'' would commit horrid, obscure sexual acts and ''incite widespread raging orgies'' until their sudden disappearance. These orgies would last anywhere from a few hours to a few months, and more often than not, left a wake of unprecedented abominations and madness. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''Ring of Vhl'Attar''] <br><br> Too large to fit any human finger, this object resembles a circle of interlaced metals with sharp spikes protruding as if to harm its wielder. Because of vast inconsistencies in the recording of its full size, some suspect it may be capable of altering its dimensions. <br><br> Interacting with the Ring can result in the inter-actor becoming 'Anointed', granting them extraordinary power. Some believe this process to be random, while others insist there is a method or criteria. Once empowered, ''they have until 6 new moons to invoke Vhl'Attar and open a gateway to his void. To do this, they attempt to create an area of high sexual concentration within a local space. ''After the 6th new moon, their power quickly wanes. All have vanished shortly after, with one account describing a creeping darkness and strong sulphuric smell. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''The Anointed''] <br><br> The Anointed are all young men. There has been a singular instance of a female, turned Affected //Ph'tanari//, growing more powerful than their sire, only to be slain in the following hour. <br><br> In most cases, something or someone slays the Anointed before the 2nd new moon. As of this writing, no Anointed have reached the 3rd, due largely to meddling from a rival cult proclaiming themselves //The Black Brothers//. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''Powers''] <br><br> * ''Edging increases the Anointed's libido, which will increase the size and volume of their phallus''. A higher libido means stronger power. * ''Orgasming decreases libido, which will decrease the size and volume of their phallus''. Some may see this as necessary, as the growing sexual energy given off by the Anointed's libido is detectable by The Black Brothers. * Anointed are immune to all known diseases transmitted via genitalia. * Sexual activity with the Anointed will ''lower the cognitive ability of their partner''. Even mere skin contact or contact with an Anointed One's ejaculate has triggered this effect. * Prolonged exposure to an Anointed can lead to high levels of arousal, but as long as no major symptoms are present, even the smallest break in exposure can be enough to escape their influence. People under this influence are called the ''Affected''. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''The Affected''] <br><br> People who fall under the influence of an Anointed one are called "The Affected," and can be almost as dangerous as the Anointed themselves. * Affected individuals who have had their cognitive ability reduced far enough will undergo a steady change in hair color to a silvery gold, and be ''increasingly susceptible to suggestions'' made by the Anointed. * If unable to escape the Anointed's influence, the Affected will insatiably seek out anyone and everyone willing to get a release from their inevitable, intense, perpetual arousal. At this point, they no longer serve the Anointed, but directly serve Vhl'Attar. * ''Women who ingest the semen of an Anointed will notice significant expansion in their breast size'', further increasing their overall libido. * There have been cases where ''an Affected took the Anointed in their mouth'', and upon pulling back, ''the Anointed's phallus had a significant increase in size''. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''Ph'tanari''] <br><br> * The Anointed ''orgasming inside the vagina of an Affected will transform the Affected into a //ph'tanari//''. //Ph'tanari// develop phallus' and can become more powerful than their sire, with similar abilities. * ''Lustful actions with //ph'tanari// or affected males may hyper-feminize the Anointed'', weakening their power and turning them submissive. Most Anointed avoid making ph'tanari after they mistakenly create the first. <br> (text-size: 1.2)[''Ph'emboi''] <br><br> * With enough power, the Anointed can ''turn their most masculine male adversaries into lustful, feminized whores''. People refer to those affected as //ph'emboi//. * Ph'emboi are naturally submissive, but can assume a temporarily dominant role should the Anointed will it. * Ph'emboi are ''always willing to have sex'', regardless of their arousal. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''Ghouls''] <br><br> * Some Anointed opt to turn their male adversaries into //ghouls//. Ghouls display somewhat inhuman characteristics. They are pale, gaunt in virility, and somber in attitude. The contortions of their faces usually prevent clear visibility. * Ghouls do not directly affect the ritual of Vhl'Attar, but they are ''loyal and obedient, often being used for menial tasks''. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''Husks''] <br><br> * With enough power, ''an Anointed may hollow out and enter the minds of others''. These people become husks of their former selves. * The Anointed may exert influence over several husks at a time. * Some Anointed perform a special ritual to ''steal parts of, or completely take over, the bodies of husks''. *Similar to ghouls, ''husks can be used for basic tasks'', but their neutered brains restrict their abilities to tasks that are physical and repetitive. <br><br> (text-size: 1.2)[''Forbidden Acts''] <br><br> * Followers of Vhl'Attar see sex for procreation, or ''vaginal sex'' between a man and a woman, as pure and explicitly forbid it. * Should the Anointed choose to engage in this type of sex, Vhl'Attar will perverse the Affected immediately afterward, ''sprouting the clitoris into a full penis to create a Ph'tanari''. This effect appears to be carried out through the Anointed's own ejaculate, which has resulted in some Anointed individuals ''using sheepskin as a protective barrier''. <br><br> (text-size: 1.8)[''The Broodmother''] <br> //The Petulant Parasite// <br><br> The Broodmother is a completely separate entity from Vhl'Attar; they are never mentioned together in the texts. It is an unpredictable wildcard with seemingly no ambition but to thrive in chaos. There are no known worshippers. Some say it rides across the cosmos by attaching itself to larger entities. * The Broodmother excels in rapidly ''reproducing swarms of mind-hijacking parasites'', but seems to lack the patience or the ability to orchestrate much of anything short of an outburst. As a result, The Broodmother tends to be quickly identified and dealt with. * ''Women'' who are in the presence of The Broodmother for a prolongued period of time may become entranced, being ''bestowed with hyper fertility''. Their offspring, however, are parasitic abominations. ''Women should avoid contact with The Broodmother at all costs''. * After birth, these writhing parasites seek out a human host, providing them with ''a major increase in libido'' at the detriment of ''losing higher cognitive functioning'' and ''muscle control''. * ''Rain'' can cause the parasites to become stronger, ''more voracious''. What began as a promising research initiative in the early 20th century ultimately led to panic, disbanded departments and organizations like Paranormal Psychology and the Occult Club, and the quiet shuttering of multiple facilities. <br><br> Today, the university has emerged as a forward-looking institution, known for its contributions to the sciences, literature, and ethics in research. But beneath the modern veneer, the past lingers- less a source of shame, and more a quiet lesson in caution and humility. <br><br> ''A Forgotten Chapter Reopened'' <br><br> Recent efforts by the University Historical Society have reignited student interest in the lesser-known corners of Miskatonic's past. Last spring, the society unveiled "The Restricted Years," a curated collection of recovered documents, personal letters, and declassified internal memos from the 1920s-1940s- a period during which multiple faculty members abruptly resigned, and research programs were inexplicably terminated. <br><br> "We're not suggesting anything supernatural," said Professor Eliza Nguyen, who advises the project. "But clearly, there were events and decisions made that shaped the trajectory of this institution in ways few students today understand." <br><br> Among the more startling discoveries were correspondences indicating growing internal concern over ethically ambiguous research into human cognition, sensory deprivation, and theoretical models of reality. Several student testimonies from the era speak of "psychological breaks," erratic faculty behavior, and prolonged isolation studies that were quietly dismissed without public explanation. <br><br> ''The Long Silence'' <br><br> In 1931, the university formally locked and sealed the Lower Archive Vaults, citing "environmental instability and archival decay." For decades, access to those facilities was restricted even to staff, and their existence faded from public memory. Some whispered that it had more to do with experimental failures than mold or structural risk- but no official explanation has ever been offered. <br><br> Following that decision, the university began distancing itself from all fields considered "speculative metaphysics," folding several departments into broader liberal arts disciplines or closing them altogether. A campus once famous for unorthodox inquiry redirected its focus to more empirical and measurable fields. <br><br> ''Reconciling the Past'' <br><br> For today's students, the strange history of Miskatonic may seem like an academic footnote- but for some, it's a key part of understanding the institution's identity. <br><br> "There's a tendency to sweep the weird stuff under the rug," said Jordan White (Class of '86), a political science major and member of the historical society. "But the fact that this place went through something so disruptive- and came out the other side- says a lot about the strength of the academic community here." <br><br> In the last decade, a growing movement has called for transparency, reflection, and, in some cases, accountability. Student-led panels now discuss the legacy of research ethics at Miskatonic, and new courses explore how institutions navigate moments of cultural or scientific crisis. <br><br> ''A University Transformed'' <br><br> Modern Miskatonic is a very different place. The old basements remain sealed, now monitored by environmental engineering for potential remediation. The once-taboo subjects of consciousness, reality, and altered perception are now approached through psychology, neuroscience, and philosophy, under strict oversight and modern ethical standards. <br><br> Annual "Reflection Weeks" give the community space to explore the past-not with fear, but with empathy and curiosity. Students visit the Hall of Archives exhibit, write letters to future scholars, and attend guided tours of old faculty lodges that once hosted controversial seminars. <br><br> ''What We Choose to Remember'' <br><br> The truth about what happened during those decades may never be fully known. But in a way, that mystery has become part of Miskatonic's culture- not as a cautionary tale, but as a reminder that the pursuit of knowledge must always be grounded in care, context, and responsibility. <br><br> As the university steps confidently into its next century, we do so carrying the lessons of the past- not buried, but acknowledged. What remains beneath may never be uncovered, but what rises above is a campus committed to reflection, integrity, and growth. ] } { (set: _sub to false, _showSearch to false, _showKickedOut to false) (if: $broodmothers contains "librarian")[ (set: _sub to true) ] (else-if: $librarian's 19th >=$thresholds's 1st)[ (set: _sub to true) ] (display:"passageText") (replace:?passageText)[ Among the dusty tomes and ancient manuscripts, you follow along the shelves with your finger until you reach the spot of the Voynitch manuscript. Witnesses have described a large animal charging from the undergrowth, though accounts differ considerably about its appearance. <br><br> ''Snarling Outside Dorm Windows'' <br><br> Residents say the encounters were preceded by occasional snarling from the woods behind the dormitories. Initially dismissed as a stray dog, the sound has reportedly been heard on several evenings over the past two weeks. <br><br> "It sounds close enough to be right beneath your window," said junior Leah Mercer. "Then someone switches on the outside lights and it bolts. We've never actually seen what's making it." <br><br> ''Attacks Along the Campus Shortcut'' <br><br> Three students have sought treatment for injuries sustained while returning from campus after dark. One reported being knocked off the path; another escaped with torn clothing and deep scratches after climbing over a fallen tree. <br><br> The description of a "rabid moose" originated with a student who recalled seeing what appeared to be antlers above the brush. Other witnesses could not confirm that detail. All described hearing a low snarl immediately before the animal approached. <br><br> ''Searches Yield Few Answers'' <br><br> Campus security has conducted daylight searches with local wildlife personnel, but no animal has been located. Rabies has not been confirmed, and officials are unable to identify a species based on the available accounts. <br><br> Students are being encouraged to use the longer, illuminated route along the access road. Security patrols have increased near the dormitories, although residents say the sounds sometimes begin again shortly after officers leave. <br><br> ''Questions About Recent Disappearances'' <br><br> The reports have renewed concern about students who have disappeared in recent weeks. Friends of one missing student say the wooded path was their usual route home from evening classes. <br><br> Police have not announced any connection between the disappearances and the attacks. They have asked anyone who heard unusual sounds near University Woods on the nights in question to come forward. ] }{ (replace:?dialogueBox)+(t8n: "fade")+(t8n-time: 2s)[ "Fine.
